questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has not sought an extension or other relief from the Board. Which continuing education plan satisfies the annual requirements?

choices.text: Five live hours, including one hour of pharmacy law, plus 15 home-study hours with no additional pharmacy-law content
Four live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 16 home-study hours
Six live hours, including one hour of pharmacy law, plus 14 home-study hours that include one hour of pharmacy law
Nine live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 10 home-study hours
Three live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 17 home-study hours

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist properly counted several courses toward last year's continuing education requirement. Eighteen months after completing the earliest course, the Board selects the pharmacist for a random audit. Which statements correctly describe the pharmacist's documentation duties? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist must retain acceptable documentation for at least two years from each course's completion date.
The pharmacist must produce the documentation when the Board requests it during the random audit.
The documentation must identify the provider and participant and include the program title or number, completion date, and hours awarded.
The two-year retention period begins at the end of the biennial pharmacist-registration cycle.
The pharmacist's renewal attestation replaces the underlying course records once the hours have been credited.

questions.stem: A provider plans a Massachusetts pharmacist continuing education program in 10 days. It did not submit the ordinary provider application 30 days before presentation, but it gives the Board acceptable documentation that its ACPE program approval is current and that it remains in good standing. Which conclusion is most accurate?

choices.text: The provider cannot be recognized because every provider must use the 30-day application route for every program.
The provider is recognized only if the Board conducts a new substantive review of the course before presentation.
The provider may be considered authorized through the current-approval and good-standing documentation route.
Only current AMA CME Category 1 approval can support that route; ACPE approval cannot.
The provider's institutional name alone would have been enough, so the approval and good-standing documents are immaterial.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts certified pharmacy technician encounters an unresolved drug-utilization-review alert. A written pharmacy protocol says that a certified technician may close the alert after checking two objective data fields, and the pharmacist is available by telephone. What is the most appropriate next step?

choices.text: Close the alert under the protocol because certification permits protocol-based clinical decisions.
Close the alert now and obtain the pharmacist's electronic cosignature after dispensing.
Call the prescriber and negotiate a therapy change under the store's escalation protocol before routing the prescription to the pharmacist.
Collect permitted objective information, but refer the unresolved clinical conflict and final decision to the pharmacist.
Read a scripted risk statement to the patient and treat that communication as resolution of the alert.

questions.stem: With the pharmacist on duty's approval, a Massachusetts certified pharmacy technician identifies themself by title before speaking with a prescriber's office about an existing patient. Which actions may the certified technician perform? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Request authorization for another refill of an existing prescription.
Receive a missing quantity for a prescription already transmitted to the pharmacy.
Recommend and accept a higher dose in response to the patient's recent symptoms.
Resolve a drug-utilization-review alert raised by the pharmacy system.
Counsel the patient on how to manage adverse effects from the medication.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician's license has been expired for 26 months. The technician submits the renewal form and fees, but the Board has not renewed the license or decided whether to impose additional conditions. The pharmacy wants the technician to begin work under direct pharmacist supervision. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: Submitting the form and fees restores the license provisionally while the Board reviews the application.
Direct pharmacist supervision may permit practice during the renewal review despite the expired license.
A lapse exceeding two years automatically requires a specified national technician examination before renewal.
The technician cannot practice until renewal; because the lapse exceeded two years, additional Board conditions may apply.
A lapse exceeding two years permanently bars renewal of the technician license.

questions.stem: One Massachusetts pharmacist is supervising one certified pharmacy technician and two pharmacy technicians. Another employee holds a current pharmacy technician license but is assigned only to the front register and initially performs no professional pharmacy support. During a rush, the manager directs that employee to enter prescription data. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: While the employee performs only cashier duties and no professional pharmacy support, the employee may be excluded from the support-personnel ratio.
Once the employee begins prescription data entry, the cashier label no longer keeps the employee outside the ratio.
The resulting four-person support team is permitted because every member holds a pharmacy personnel credential.
The employee remains excluded for the entire shift because the schedule lists the employee as a cashier.
The data-entry assignment must satisfy technician scope and supervision rules independently of the numerical ratio analysis.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist's personal registration expired 61 days ago. It has never been suspended or revoked. The pharmacist pays the renewal and late fees this morning and asks to begin a shift while the Board processes the renewal. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The pharmacist falls within the 60-day fee-only branch and may practice once payment is submitted.
Any lapse beyond 60 days automatically requires passage of the MPJE before renewal.
Direct oversight by another pharmacist permits practice until the registration is renewed.
Board conditions may apply, but the over-two-year MPJE branch does not; practice must wait for renewal.
The registration remains effective for six months after expiration if all continuing education was completed on time.

questions.stem: An applicant for Massachusetts pharmacist licensure submits a birth record under a former surname and uses a current married surname on the application. The applicant otherwise appears eligible but does not include written notice of the name change. What is the best assessment?

choices.text: The applicant should provide written notice of the name change because substantive eligibility does not cure an incomplete application.
The application is complete because the Board must infer the name change from the different surnames.
A current government-issued photo identification automatically replaces the required birth record and written name-change notice for all licensure purposes.
The discrepancy matters only after the applicant passes all required examinations.
The applicant must abandon the current surname and apply only under the surname shown on the birth record.

questions.stem: A community pharmacy receives an individually signed referral for a patient to enter a collaborative drug therapy management program. The document lists the patient's name and address, primary diagnosis, authorized comorbid diagnoses, and detailed treatment instructions. It does not state the patient's known allergies and contains no statement that the patient gave written informed consent. The pharmacist notes that the affiliated hospital often begins inpatient collaborative management through a consultation request that does not contain those two items. What is the best conclusion for the community-pharmacy referral?

choices.text: It is sufficient because a signed referral and specific treatment instructions replace the need for allergy and consent information.
It is sufficient if the hospital's consultation process would accept the same document.
It is incomplete because a community CDTM referral must include known allergies and a statement of written informed consent, in addition to the other required patient-specific information.
It is incomplete only if the patient has a known allergy that would change the treatment instructions.
It may be completed by treating the hospital's consultation request as an incorporated attachment, even though that request contains neither missing item.

questions.stem: During prospective drug utilization review, the pharmacy system flags a clinically significant conflict. A certified pharmacy technician tells the pharmacist that the technician can clear the alert under the pharmacy's protocol and that documentation is needed only if the prescriber is called. Which statements correctly describe the Massachusetts requirements? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist must determine what measures are appropriate in response to the DUR finding and may choose consultation with the prescriber, the patient, or the patient's agent when appropriate.
The pharmacist must document the measures taken in response to the DUR finding, not only a prescriber call.
A certified pharmacy technician may resolve the clinical conflict independently when an approved protocol supplies the decision steps.
Every DUR finding requires prescriber consultation before dispensing, regardless of the pharmacist's clinical assessment.
Documentation is optional when the pharmacist addresses the issue directly with the patient rather than the prescriber.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy delivers a prescription to a patient's home. A toll-free number connects the patient to a pharmacist during the pharmacy's regular hours, but the number appears only on the delivery receipt and not on the prescription container label. The pharmacy's record contains no entry showing that the patient failed to accept an offer to counsel. Which conclusion best separates the two legal issues?

choices.text: The remote-delivery requirement is satisfied by the receipt, and the absent refusal record creates no presumption.
The label placement fails the remote-delivery requirement, but the absent failure-to-accept record creates the statutory presumption that counseling was provided.
The missing label number defeats both remote access compliance and the statutory counseling presumption.
The remote-delivery requirement is satisfied whenever a pharmacist is reachable, but counseling is presumed not to have occurred without an affirmative counseling note.
The statutory presumption applies only if the toll-free number appears on both the receipt and the container label.

questions.stem: A pharmacy manager audits a consultation space. Patients can enter it from the public side without passing through the dispensing area or stockroom. The opening has a waist-high divider, ordinary conversations can be heard in the waiting line, and a small sign reads "Counseling Room." Which changes are needed to satisfy the Massachusetts consultation-area requirements? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Display prominent signage designating the space as the "Patient Consultation Area."
Add features that provide visual privacy for consultations.
Add sound-control features sufficient to provide auditory privacy.
Relocate the space so patients must enter through the dispensing area before each consultation.
Replace privacy features with a staff escort whenever sensitive information will be discussed.

questions.stem: A hospital pharmacy does not hold a Drug Store license. A hospital employee asks it to fill an outpatient prescription for the employee's spouse. The spouse has lived at a separate address for six months and is not a hospital patient. What is the best conclusion under the Massachusetts institutional-dispensing rule?

choices.text: The pharmacy may dispense because legal marriage alone places the spouse within the employee-family category.
The pharmacy may dispense if the employee promises to deliver the medication personally.
The pharmacy may not rely on the employee-spouse exception because the spouse does not reside in the same household as the employee.
The pharmacy may dispense because household status matters only for an employee's child, not a spouse.
The pharmacy may dispense any outpatient prescription written by a hospital practitioner, regardless of the recipient.

questions.stem: Without patient authorization or another identified legal basis, a pharmacist sends a patient's complete medication profile through an encrypted portal to the patient's employer. The employer requested the profile for a workplace wellness review. Which statement best applies the Massachusetts licensee confidentiality duty?

choices.text: Encryption makes the transmission permissible because confidentiality duties address only accidental public exposure.
The pharmacist violates the affirmative confidentiality duty by sending the profile to an unauthorized recipient, despite using a secure channel.
The disclosure is permissible because an employer may request any medication information connected with a wellness program.
No confidentiality issue exists unless the employer later forwards the profile to someone else.
The duty is satisfied whenever the pharmacy protects its stored copy of the profile from unauthorized access.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed manufacturer injection training and has safely used the same device in another licensed role. The pharmacy now asks the pharmacist to administer a prescription product that is not on the Department's current eligible-medication list and does not fall within another recognized Massachusetts pharmacist-administration pathway. Which conclusions are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Device training may support personal competence, but it does not add the product to the legally recognized administration scope.
Demonstrated technical skill alone authorizes administration of any prescription injectable.
The pharmacist must satisfy both the individual education, training, and experience standard and the applicable legal scope for the product and act.
Placement of the product on the pharmacy's internal protocol is equivalent to inclusion in the Department's eligible-medication guidance.
On these facts, the pharmacist should not administer the product solely on the strength of prior device experience.

questions.stem: A pharmacist lawfully administers an eligible medication under the applicable Massachusetts pathway. A temporary system outage prevents immediate electronic transmission of the administration record, so the pharmacist sends it to the prescriber at the next practical opportunity after service is restored. How should the timing language in the current Department guidance be characterized?

choices.text: It is a statutory SHALL deadline that automatically invalidates the administration under Massachusetts law if the record is not transmitted immediately.
It is nonmandatory guidance strongly encouraging transmission as soon after administration as practical, not a validity condition.
It prohibits any administration unless the prescriber confirms receipt of the record in advance.
It makes prescriber communication entirely irrelevant once the medication has been administered.
It requires transmission by the end of the same calendar day without regard to practical system limitations.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a warfarin prescription issued 20 days ago by a Rhode Island practitioner who is properly licensed and registered as required. Massachusetts treats warfarin as Schedule VI. The pharmacist independently judges the prescription to be authentic and valid. A colleague says Massachusetts nevertheless requires separate telephone verification of every out-of-state Schedule III through VI prescription. What is the best response?

choices.text: The colleague is correct because the separate verification mandate applies identically to Schedules III, IV, V, and VI whenever a prescription was issued outside Massachusetts.
The prescription is barred because any out-of-state Schedule VI prescription must be filled within 7 days.
The prescription may be considered within the 30-day III-VI window if judged authentic and valid; separate prescriber verification applies to Schedules III-V, not Schedule VI.
Schedule VI prescriptions from another state require no pharmacist authenticity or validity judgment.
The prescription becomes a federal Schedule V prescription when presented across state lines, so the Schedule III-V verification rule applies.

questions.stem: A patient returns a liquid medication that the pharmacy had correctly dispensed. The patient reports that it developed unexpected particles before the labeled expiration date, and the pharmacist reasonably suspects contamination. Which actions or conclusions are required under the Massachusetts return rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Accept the returned medication even though the original dispensing was not erroneous.
Decline the return because a pharmacy must accept only medications that it dispensed in error.
Keep the returned medication out of active inventory and quarantine it from usable stock.
Dispose of the returned medication through the appropriate process rather than redispensing it.
Treat the return like an ordinary nondefective therapy-change return, for which acceptance is always mandatory.

questions.stem: A pharmacy wants its pharmacists to inject a prescription medication that falls outside the Massachusetts statutory pharmacist-administration pathways applicable to the planned service. Its written workflow first labels the event a completed dispensing, has the patient take possession of the prefilled device for several seconds, and then has the pharmacist inject the same medication in the consultation room. Internal emails state that the temporary transfer was added so the injection would not appear to be pharmacist administration. What is the best conclusion?

choices.text: The workflow is permissible because each formally labeled step can be described without using the word administration.
The temporary transfer of possession automatically converts the pharmacist's injection into patient self-administration.
The workflow is prohibited because a licensee may not directly or indirectly arrange formal steps intended to circumvent a restriction on pharmacist administration.
The workflow is permissible whenever the medication was lawfully prescribed and dispensed before the injection.
Only the prescriber, not the pharmacist licensee, can be responsible for circumvention in an administration service.

questions.stem: A pharmacy prepared and labeled a prescription, but the patient never picked it up and the medication was never dispensed. The pharmacy is evaluating whether to return the medication to stock under 247 CMR 9.13. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The never-dispensed medication may be returned to stock if the rule's container, labeling, expiration, and recall safeguards are satisfied.
The medication may be poured back into the manufacturer's stock bottle because the patient never possessed it.
It may remain in the original patient container, or be placed in an appropriate container bearing the required product identifiers and the expiration date assigned when the prescription was filled.
The pharmacy must maintain procedures that permit identification and removal of the returned-to-stock medication if it is later recalled.
Once prepared for a patient, the medication is treated as previously dispensed even when it never left the pharmacy, so return to stock is categorically barred.

questions.stem: A patient asks a Massachusetts pharmacy to obtain a prescription issued 13 months ago for a prescription-only drug that is not listed in Schedules I through V. The prescription record shows two authorized refills remaining. Which statements should the receiving pharmacist apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The remaining refills keep the prescription transferable until both have been dispensed.
The drug falls within Massachusetts Schedule VI because it is a prescription drug not otherwise placed in Schedules I through V.
The transfer must be declined because a Schedule VI prescription may not be transferred more than one year after issuance.
The transfer may proceed, but the receiving pharmacy must apply the federal six-month refill period for Schedule III through V prescriptions.
The rule allowing Schedule VI prescriptions to transfer in the same manner as Schedule III through V prescriptions does not displace the separate one-year transfer ceiling.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is revising the pickup procedure. One prescription is for an ordinary Schedule VI drug that has not been designated by the Commissioner for the additional-drug identification requirement. Another is for a drug that has received that formal designation. Which statements correctly describe the Customer Identifier rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The designated additional drug is within the Customer Identifier rule even though it is not described as a Schedule II through V drug.
Every Schedule VI dispensing is within the rule because Massachusetts calls Schedule VI a controlled-substance schedule.
Dispensing a controlled substance in Schedule II, III, IV, or V is within the rule's stated scope.
The ordinary Schedule VI drug is not brought within the rule merely by its Schedule VI classification.
A familiar customer may receive a covered drug without identification or the documented hardship procedure.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist dispenses a prescription drug distributed solely under its generic name. The product has no NDC number, and the manufacturer's name cannot be identified from the product or available records. The name of the repacker is available. What should the pharmacist record in the computerized pharmacy system?

choices.text: Only the generic drug name, because no NDC number exists.
The prescriber's name as the substitute product identifier.
The wholesaler's invoice number, regardless of who packaged the product.
The repacker's name, because the NDC and manufacturer-name steps are unavailable.
No product-identity entry, provided the pharmacist documents why the NDC is missing.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacy receives a medication after prescription processing was performed outside its premises at another pharmacy licensed by the Massachusetts Board. No separate Massachusetts pharmacist re-verifies that offsite processing at the receiving pharmacy. The pharmacist on duty inspects the finished medication before dispensing. Which assessment is most accurate?

choices.text: Dispensing is prohibited because every offsite process must be separately re-verified at the receiving pharmacy.
The Board-licensed offsite pharmacy satisfies an alternative condition for dispensing, without treating the final inspection as verification of the process.
The final inspection alone satisfies the rule, whether or not the offsite pharmacy is licensed by the Board.
The medication may be dispensed only if the offsite pharmacy also shares ownership with the receiving pharmacy.
The medication may be dispensed because any pharmacy license issued by any jurisdiction satisfies the offsite-site condition.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy partially fills a Schedule II prescription at the patient's request two days after the prescription was issued. On day 29 after issuance, the patient asks a different pharmacy to dispense the balance because the first pharmacy is closed. On day 31, the patient returns to the first pharmacy for the balance. Which assessment is correct?

choices.text: The second pharmacy may dispense the balance on day 29 because the federal 30-day period has not expired.
The first pharmacy may dispense the balance on day 31 because the 30 days run from the initial partial fill.
Either pharmacy may dispense the balance if it can access the original prescription electronically.
Neither requested dispensing is permitted: only the pharmacy that made the partial fill may dispense the balance, and it must do so no later than 30 days after issuance.
Neither requested dispensing is permitted because every Schedule II remainder is due within 72 hours of the partial fill.

questions.stem: During a documented medical emergency, a Massachusetts pharmacy receives a prescription that is not marked 'no substitution.' The brand product written by the prescriber is in stock, but no less expensive interchangeable product is available. Which actions are part of the permitted emergency pathway? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Dispense the brand product as written despite the usual interchange direction.
Ask the prescriber to add a no-substitution direction before using the emergency pathway.
Record the date, hour, and nature of the medical emergency on the prescription or in the computerized pharmacy system.
Treat the pharmacist's notation as sufficient evidence that the purchaser accepted the deviation.
Obtain the purchaser's written indication that the purchaser accepts the deviation.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist reviews a written Schedule II prescription before dispensing. The prescription contains the required patient, drug, strength, directions, and date information and bears the prescriber's signature, but it omits the practitioner's registration number. The filling pharmacist has already signed the face of the prescription. What is the best assessment?

choices.text: The prescription is complete because the pharmacist's face endorsement supplies the missing registration element.
The prescription is complete because a practitioner's signature makes a separate registration number unnecessary.
The pharmacist's endorsement satisfies the pharmacist's own duty but does not cure the missing practitioner registration number.
The missing registration number is cured if a second pharmacist countersigns the face before dispensing.
The registration number may be omitted from Schedule II prescriptions because they cannot be refilled.

questions.stem: The pharmacist manager of a Massachusetts pharmacy that holds a standard pharmacy license and a complex non-sterile compounding license plans to begin preparing a hazardous sterile preparation for individual patients. Which conclusions should guide the plan? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacy must satisfy the specialty-licensure gate applicable to sterile compounding before beginning the activity.
The preparation remains subject to the sterile-compounding framework even though its hazardous status adds another layer of controls.
The complex non-sterile compounding license covers the activity because it is a specialty compounding license.
Current hazardous-drug handling requirements apply in addition to the sterile-compounding requirements.
Patient-specific preparation removes the specialty-licensure gate and leaves only hazardous-drug handling requirements.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy holds only a standard pharmacy license. Its manager proposes to prepare a complex non-sterile product that requires specialized facilities and training. A commercially available product could meet the patient's clinical needs, but the compounded product would cost less. The prescriber identifies no difference other than price. Which conclusion is most accurate?

choices.text: The standard pharmacy license is sufficient because lower price is a significant clinical difference.
The pharmacy needs the complex non-sterile compounding license, but lower price alone establishes a significant clinical difference.
Patient-specific preparation removes the specialty-license requirement, although price alone is not a significant clinical difference.
The standard license is sufficient if the prescriber documents that the price difference is important to the patient.
The proposal cannot proceed as described because the complex activity requires the appropriate specialty license and price alone is not a significant clinical difference.

questions.stem: During a required controlled-substance inventory, a pharmacist reviews several opened containers. Which counting decisions comply with the federal inventory rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Use an estimated count for an opened bottle labeled as containing 240 Schedule II tablets.
Use an estimated count for an opened bottle labeled as containing 900 Schedule III tablets.
Use an estimated count for an opened bottle labeled as containing 900 Schedule IV tablets.
Determine the exact count in an opened bottle labeled as containing 1,200 Schedule V capsules.
Determine the exact count in an opened bottle labeled as containing 80 Schedule II capsules.

questions.stem: A pharmacy is revising its electronic records for Schedule I and II procurement. The system contains electronic copies of DEA Forms 222 as well as orders executed through the Controlled Substance Ordering System (CSOS). Which conclusions are accurate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A paper Form 222 may be filed with all other pharmacy records as long as staff can locate it with a keyword search.
An electronic copy of a Form 222 may be stored with other records if it is readily retrievable separately from those records.
A digitally signed CSOS order is an alternative ordering record, not merely an electronic copy of a Form 222.
Scanning a completed paper Form 222 converts it into a CSOS order.
The rule governing preservation of CSOS electronic orders is distinct from the rule governing storage of electronic Form 222 copies.

questions.stem: A newly registered pharmacy begins dispensing operations on Monday but has no controlled substances in stock. Its first controlled-substance shipment is expected on Friday. What should the pharmacist in charge do about the federal initial inventory?

choices.text: Wait until Friday and treat the arriving shipment record as the initial inventory.
Create the initial inventory on Monday and record that no controlled substances are then on hand.
Do not create an initial inventory because the requirement begins only after a controlled substance is received.
Ask the wholesaler to create the pharmacy's initial inventory when the first order is shipped.
Use the first biennial inventory as both the initial inventory and the record of Friday's shipment.
